original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Exact joint first-pivot law for an arbitrary finite family of rank-one projectors sharing a complete GL_m(F_q) header, over every finite field, with the explicit seven-type law for two requests.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a proof audit. This contribution instead answers #4239's open question 1 with a new counting law for a changed shared-header interface; it does not recheck #4100 or #4239.
bottleneck_link: Side result for possible header reuse: it determines exactly how nonorthogonal rank-one requests constrain one shared header. No physical cost saving or actual supplier binding is claimed.
stop_rule: Stop at the rank-one joint law and bounded finite corroboration; no higher-rank joint law, physical supplier or recurrence repricing.
evidence: Written inclusion-exclusion proof; exhaustive ordered-pair census over eight (q,m) domains including F4; complete-conjugation GL census over four domains; seeded random three- and four-request families; six controls; generated RESULT.json binds exact bytes.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the joint full-guard law for nonorthogonal requests of rank greater than one?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Actual BIT requests have rank r with leading-pivot guards, not only rank one.
open_questions.first_step: Start with two rank-two requests at m=3 or 4 over F3, using #4228's Schur-complement recurrence for one request and this package's inclusion-exclusion for the cross terms.
open_questions.blocked_by: The guard is no longer a product of two linear forms, so the subspace-pairing count used here does not apply directly.

open_questions.question: Does an actual producer emit a request family whose rank data make one shared header useful?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The algebraic law gives no saving until a caller's selection, emission, dispatch, dirty return and stock are charged.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one producer, read off its image/kernel ranks and Gram blocks, and price the complete shared-header caller.
open_questions.blocked_by: No actual request family or physical caller has been bound.

coordination.coverage: Open PR titles (100 most recent), this account's PRs, last 30 handoff comments, find_overlap.py for uniform-transfer-audit, and merged README greps for nonorthogonal/joint header/tr(PQ) terms. Closed history and code-diff coverage partial.
